name: CHILE

flag.title: Flag of Chile
flag.note: Red, white & blue with lone star

lead: Chile is a long, thin ribbon of land down the west edge of South America. You can drive from the Pacific Ocean to the Andes in just hours. Yet it has every climate on Earth. The north has the world's driest desert. The far south has glaciers and penguins.
geo: Chile is the world's longest, thinnest country. It is 4,300 km long and never more than 350 km wide. The Atacama Desert gets less than 1 mm of rain a year, drier than Mars.
Patagonia, in the south, has crashing glaciers and jade fjords. Easter Island is part of Chile too. This tiny dot lies 3,700 km out in the South Pacific.
animals: Andean flamingos wade in salt lakes so shallow they look like pink mirrors. The Andean condor has a 3-metre wingspan. It soars above the peaks for hours without one flap.
Magellanic penguins swim in the cold Humboldt Current with sea lions and dolphins. The pudú, the world's tiniest deer, is only 35 cm tall.
culture: Chileans love empanadas, pastry pockets filled with beef, olives and egg. Their national sport is rodeo. Horsemen called huasos herd a calf around a ring.
Chile has two Nobel Prize poets, Pablo Neruda and Gabriela Mistral. Neruda built three odd houses, and one looks like a ship. Cueca dancers wave handkerchiefs like courting birds.
history: The Mapuche people lived here long before Europeans came. They famously resisted the Inca. Spain founded Santiago in 1541. Chile won independence in 1818 under Bernardo O'Higgins.
A socialist government began in 1970. A military coup followed in 1973 and lasted until democracy returned in 1990.
wows: Chile is 4,300 km long but only 177 km wide on average.
Some Atacama weather stations have never recorded a drop of rain.
Chile produces about one-third of the world's copper.
Ojos del Salado is the world's highest active volcano at 6,893 m.
Easter Island's moai statues were moved without wheels or metal tools.
The pudú is the world's smallest deer, just 35 cm tall.
Chile's coastline is 6,435 km, as far as London to New York.

myths.myth: The Atacama is the hottest desert on Earth
myths.fact: It is the driest, not the hottest. Its nights can be chilly.

myths.myth: Easter Island statues are only heads
myths.fact: The moai have full bodies. Most are buried up to their necks.
